item.title: Fixing Browser Extension Injections on Dynamic YouTube Page Transitions
item.description:
“Fixing Browser Extension Injections on Dynamic YouTube Page Transitions”

Detecting Dynamic Page Transitions on YouTube

The core challenge is that YouTube avoids traditional page refreshes for internal navigation. This means events like DOMContentLoaded or standard content script injection triggers only happen on the initial load. To address this, we must hook into YouTube’s custom event system or utilize browser extension APIs.

Method 1: Utilizing YouTube’s Internal Navigation Events

By inspecting the Document Object Model (DOM) events available in the developer console using getEventListeners(document), specific events related to YouTube’s internal navigation system can be identified.
